home.title: CelikPanel · Hosting control panel for Linux servers
home.description: CelikPanel is a hosting control panel for Linux servers: websites, mail, DNS, databases and backups, run as the system’s own services. Systems, customer separation, measurements, licence and release on one page.
home.h1: A hosting control panel for Linux servers
home.def: It manages websites, mail, DNS, databases and backups with the server’s own services, so sites, mail, DNS and databases keep running when the panel stops.

home.sep.title: Separation between customers
home.sep.text: What keeps one account from reaching another, and what is not done yet.
home.sep.caption: Separation between accounts, as the release notes up to 0.1.0-alpha.145 state it
home.sep.note: Not yet: not in any published release. The sandbox’s escape tests on every supported system are still open in the lab.
sep.account: Each site has its own system account, and its PHP runs as that account
sep.sandbox: Node.js sites, Python apps and uploaded programs (optional programs) run in a sandbox under the site’s own account; existing Node.js sites move in when the administrator moves them
sep.logins: Extra FTP and SFTP logins see one folder of their site and never a command line
sep.names: No customer or reseller can take another account’s domain name or site account, or a port of the server’s own services (names that overlapped before alpha.142 are listed for the administrator)
sep.links: A link in a site’s folder does not serve another account’s files
sep.restore: SQL from a backup, a copy or an import runs with the database owner’s rights, not the administrator’s
sep.postgres: PostgreSQL databases are closed to other accounts: new ones from the start; older ones by the panel after a day in which no other account was seen using them, otherwise when the administrator closes them on the PostgreSQL page
sep.signing: Outgoing mail is signed only for the sender’s own domain (not yet on Arch Linux, whose OpenDKIM cannot tie signing to the login)
sep.mail: Outgoing mail limits per mailbox, domain and hosting account (optional; off until the administrator turns them on)
sep.php: PHP and scheduled tasks in the site’s own sandbox
sep.limits: Processor and memory limits per account for all of its programs (today: PHP memory, run time and process count per site)
sep.visible: Hiding which other sites exist: account names and processes are still visible to a site account

download.title: Install · CelikPanel
download.description: Install CelikPanel on a clean Linux server with one command: the signed release, the supported systems, the setup wizard and how the panel changes your server.
download.def: One command on a clean Linux server downloads the signed release, checks it and installs the panel. Go, Node.js or Git are not needed.
download.spec.label: The release this page installs
download.spec.package.v: One archive for Linux amd64, with its SHA-256 and a signed manifest
download.steps.title: Steps
download.steps.text: Start on a clean test server you can reinstall.
download.systems.title: Systems
download.systems.text: Tried on every release candidate, or supported.
download.systems.more: What each system offers, and how its updates work
download.wizard.title: Setup wizard
download.wizard.text: On first sign-in it asks for the main domain and where DNS lives. It shows its plan and changes nothing until you start it.
download.wizard.caption: Where DNS lives
download.wizard.own.text: The server keeps its own DNS, with BIND or PowerDNS. One server is enough.
download.wizard.outside.text: No DNS software is installed. The panel shows the records to add at your provider and what the internet answers for each; it does not write to the provider.
download.wizard.two.text: The second server keeps a copy of the DNS. It joins with a code that is shown once and is valid for 24 hours. Each server has its own licence.
download.how.title: How CelikPanel changes your server
download.how.caption: Rules for changes
download.how.confirm.text: Server changes (installing components, the setup wizard, updates) show what they will do and wait for your confirmation.
download.how.once.text: A repeated click or a resent request never runs a change twice.
download.how.one.text: Server-wide changes (installs, setup, updates) run one at a time; another waits or is refused until the first ends.
download.how.native.text: Sites, mail, DNS and databases run as the system’s own services and keep running when the panel stops.
download.how.kept.text: A configuration file you changed by hand is kept; CelikPanel puts its own text beside it and tells you.
download.how.split.text: The web-facing panel never runs as root. Only the local agent may change the system.
download.how.password: Your password stays on your server
download.how.password.text: The first administrator is created on your server; the password is never sent to this website.
download.installed.title: Already installed?
download.installed.text: Update from inside your panel, under Settings, CelikPanel updates. Only the owner starts it; nothing installs by itself. If an update fails after it has replaced the installed version, the panel puts back the previous version and its database by itself (changes made in the panel after the update are lost); if it stops earlier, nothing was changed. The update screen says which happened.
systems.title: Supported systems · CelikPanel
systems.description: The Linux systems CelikPanel runs on today, what each offers, what it does not and why, and how its updates work.
systems.def: CelikPanel runs on Linux servers. What is supported today, what each system offers, and how its updates work.
systems.list.title: The list
systems.list.text: Dates are the distributions’ own security support dates.
systems.list.other: Other systems are not supported yet; support for more systems is planned. Red Hat family systems (RHEL, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux 9) are recognised, and the installer refuses them for now. A system not in this table has not been checked.
systems.deb.title: Systems with apt
systems.deb.text: Debian and Ubuntu. Packages come from the distribution.
systems.deb.caption: What the apt systems offer
systems.deb.offered.text_html: CelikPanel’s components from the distribution’s own packages. Where a newer version is wanted, a vendor repository (for PHP or PostgreSQL, for example) is offered only as a deliberate choice.
systems.deb.notoffered.text_html: Apache and Exim, on any system: their integration is not finished, so use Nginx and Postfix. Versions differ by release: Debian 13 ships PHP 8.4 and PostgreSQL 17, Ubuntu 24.04 ships PHP 8.3 and PostgreSQL 16. The panel shows what your release offers.
systems.deb.updates.text_html: Fixes come from the distribution. With Automatic, the system’s own unattended-upgrades installs what it is set to take (by default the security updates) by itself every day; with Manual you install them yourself. You choose in the panel under Security; the panel shows which archives are used. The choice is one apt file, /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades, so it keeps working while CelikPanel is stopped. The panel never restarts the server by itself.
systems.deb.major.text_html: A new major version, such as PostgreSQL 17 after 16 or PHP 8.5 after 8.4, is a separate program and not an update. Updates fix the version you have; you move to a new major version yourself, when you decide.
systems.arch.title: Systems with pacman
systems.arch.text: Arch Linux, a rolling release. Only official Arch packages are used.
systems.arch.caption: What Arch Linux offers
systems.arch.offered.text: The server roles with official Arch packages: web, PHP, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, mail, certificates, the firewall and backups. Valkey is offered where other systems offer Redis.
systems.arch.notoffered: What is not offered, and why
systems.arch.notoffered.1: phpPgAdmin is not in Arch’s official repositories, and neither is SpamAssassin’s Postfix bridge (both only in the AUR, which CelikPanel does not use). Manage PostgreSQL with psql, and use Rspamd as the spam filter.
systems.arch.notoffered.2: Redis: Arch ships the compatible Valkey instead, so Valkey is offered.
systems.arch.notoffered.3: Apache and Exim: not offered yet on any system. Use Nginx and Postfix.
systems.arch.notoffered.4: Switching an existing DNS server to PowerDNS: on Arch, PowerDNS is installed only on a server with no DNS software.
systems.arch.notoffered.5: Automatic upgrades: CelikPanel schedules none on Arch.
systems.arch.updates.text_html: Every update is a full upgrade that you run on the server: read archlinux.org/news first, then run sudo pacman -Syu, then check failed units, nginx -t, PHP-FPM and the mail services, and restart the server if the kernel changed. The panel lists these steps; it never runs the upgrade for you.
systems.arch.big.text: A full upgrade can move Arch’s php and PostgreSQL packages to a new major version. Test your sites after the upgrade, or on a copy of the server first.
systems.yours.title: Independent of the panel
systems.yours.text: CelikPanel operates your server; it does not own it. On every system above, sites, mail, DNS, databases, scheduled tasks and site certificate renewal keep running while the panel is stopped.

releases.description: The current CelikPanel release with its version, date, commit, SHA-256 and signed files, and how to check a download yourself.
releases.def: Every release is signed and named by its commit. Installed panels update only when their owner starts it.
releases.files.title: Files
releases.files.text: What the installer checks, to check yourself.
releases.check.title: Check a download yourself
releases.check.text: The installer does this before it installs anything. You can repeat it by hand.
releases.check.caption: Steps
releases.check.step1: Download the package, its SHA-256 file, the signed manifest, its signature and the public key into one folder.
releases.check.step2: Compare the key’s SHA-256 with the one printed below, then check the package against its SHA-256 file.
releases.check.step3: Verify the manifest’s signature with the key.
releases.check.note: The checksum line must say “OK”, the signature line “Signature Verified Successfully”, and the last two lines must print the same SHA-256.
releases.check.key: SHA-256 of the release signing public key:
releases.update.title: Updating an installed panel
releases.update.text: Open Settings, CelikPanel updates, and start the update yourself; only the owner can. If an update fails after it has replaced the installed version, the panel puts back the previous version and its database by itself (changes made in the panel after the update are lost); if it stops earlier, nothing was changed. The update screen says which happened. Sites, mail, DNS and databases are not part of a rollback.
releases.update.notes: Each release’s notes name its commit, say what was tried in the lab and what was not, and list the known limits.

problems.description: Problems in CelikPanel that we have accepted, what to do meanwhile, and the version that fixed them; and how to report a problem.
problems.def: Problems we have accepted, in our own words, with what to do meanwhile and the version that fixed them. A security problem is listed here only after the release that closes it is published.
problems.list.title: Cases
problems.list.text: Newest first. A fixed case links to the changes of the release that fixed it.
problems.list.caption: Known problems
problems.list.note: Each case is taken from the published release notes. A report is shown here only in our own summary: never the reporter’s name, server, domain or words.
problems.report.title: Report a problem
problems.report.text: How to report today, what to include, and what happens next.
problems.report.caption: Reporting a problem
problems.report.security.text: Report it privately, never in a public issue:
problems.report.other.text: Open a report in our feedback repository on GitHub. Write nothing there that you would not publish.
problems.report.include.text: The CelikPanel version, the operating system, what you pressed, and what the screen said.
problems.report.never.text: Passwords, keys, tokens or anyone’s personal data.
problems.report.next.text: When we accept a report, it gets a number on this page, then its state, and once fixed the version that fixed it.
problems.report.form.text: There is no reporting form in the celikpanel.net account yet; report as above.
problems.states.title: What the states mean
problems.states.caption: States of a case
problems.states.looking: We have the report and are finding out what happens and why.
problems.states.accepted: It is a defect and a release will fix it; the case says what to do until then.
problems.states.fixed: The named release fixed it; update to it from the panel’s own update screen.
problems.states.not-defect: The panel works as intended; the case says why.
releases.check.step4: Compare the archive_sha256 line of the manifest with the package’s SHA-256; they must be identical. Only then is the package the signed one.
sep.webgroup: Each site with its own web-server group (today the web server’s group can read every site’s folder; the link rule is the barrier)
sep.mailmaps: Mail address lists hidden from other accounts
sep.pgmove: Moving a database to another PostgreSQL version with the owner’s rights (today: the administrator’s)
sep.webmaildoor: Webmail’s local door on the server answers only CelikPanel’s own checks, not other accounts asking for Roundcube’s files
